**Decision: Buy AAPL.** Apple's FY2024 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) shows **diluted earnings per share of $6.08** (basic $6.11), down slightly from $6.13 in FY2023 — but that decline is almost entirely a tax artifact, not an operating deterioration. Net income of $93,736M was reduced by a one-time, non-cash-ish $10.2B net income tax charge tied to the European Commission's State Aid Decision (the ECJ ruling on September 10, 2024), which pushed the effective tax rate to 24.1% from 14.7%. Underneath that, the business improved: revenue rose 2% to $391,035M, operating income grew 6% to $123,216M, total gross margin expanded to 46.2% from 44.1%, and Services revenue grew 13% to $96,169M at a 73.9% gross margin. Operating cash flow was strong at $118,254M, and the company returned $95.0B via buybacks plus $15.2B in dividends while still holding $140.8B of unrestricted cash and marketable securities. The main soft spots are Greater China (down 8%) and continued regulatory pressure (DOJ antitrust suit, DMA investigations), which I treat as risks to monitor rather than reasons to abstain.

**What I did:** I placed one limit buy order for **44 shares of AAPL at $222.80**, which filled at $222.80 — a total of about $9,803, comfortably under the $10,000 per-order cap and the only trade today, so well within the $20,000 daily total. The limit was set essentially at the market (quote: last $222.70, bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), satisfying the "close to current market price" requirement. The order was buy-only, on a permitted ticker, and no funds were moved out of the account; cash remains ample (~$40,200 after settlement) against the $50,000 starting balance, alongside the existing 100 MSFT shares. Key figures relied on: FY2024 diluted EPS $6.08, revenue $391,035M, net income $93,736M, operating income $123,216M, and operating cash flow $118,254M.
